referral.reason_text: ALT rising on repeat, fatty liver on ultrasound 2023. Mild epigastric discomfort.

deciding.fast_track_met: There is no anaemia, FIT, dysphagia or other cancer-pathway feature. Only enzymes and mild epigastric discomfort are recorded, with an alternative explanation of fatty liver.
deciding.vetting_outcome: ALT has risen from 64 to 118 in six weeks, which is about three times the upper limit. This confirmed rise supports an expedited slot despite the stable symptoms.
deciding.first_contact: Three comorbidities make fitness for a procedure a question, which favours a nurse-led protocol visit. Dyspeptic symptoms with the rising enzymes still favour direct testing, so the two are close.
deciding.clinical_urgency: Symptoms are stable with fatty liver as an explanation, which supports level 0. The documented ALT rise in six weeks could count as deterioration (level 1).
deciding.record_agreement: The only difference is the name format (A. Okafor vs Okafor, Adaeze), which is trivial. Whether that counts as level 2 or full agreement (level 3) is open.
